key_insight: FuseReg shows that the layer fusion choice in representation autoencoders is not just a design detail—it directly controls the balance between pixel-level reconstruction and high-quality generation. By regularizing fusion, the method narrows the reconstruction-generation gap and makes a single latent space work better for both tasks.
problem_solved: Representation autoencoders must choose which pretrained encoder layers to fuse into a shared latent space, but shallow layers help reconstruction while deeper layers help generation. This paper addresses how to reduce the trade-off between preserving fine image details and achieving strong generative performance.
method: Regularize the layer-fusion process so the shared latent space is optimized for both reconstruction and generation.
Encourage a better balance between shallow, detail-preserving features and deeper, generation-friendly features.
Use the fused representation as the common latent for both the generator and pixel decoder, reducing mismatch between their objectives.
impact: This matters because it helps practitioners build RAEs that do not have to sacrifice one capability for the other. The result is a more practical latent representation for image generation systems that need both faithful reconstruction and strong sample quality.

paper_title: FuseReg: Regularizing Layer Fusion Mitigates the Reconstruction-Generation Gap in Representation Autoencoders
paper_authors: Hongyang Du, Yunfei Xie, Junjie Ye, Jiawei Yang, Xiaoyan Cong
